name.text: L2 Q1 Image and running machine

questiontext.text: What is the relationship between a machine image and a virtual machine?

generalfeedback.text: An image supplies the starting state for instances. The instances can subsequently change independently; their changes do not automatically rewrite the source image.

answer.text: The image is the live machine's current CPU and memory usage.
One image can be used to initialize multiple VM instances, which can later develop different state.
Every image can initialize only one VM.
Launching a VM automatically updates the source image whenever the VM changes.

questiontext.text: What is the principal artifact produced by the AWS Packer build in demo-02?

generalfeedback.text: The Packer build prepares a temporary instance and captures a reusable AMI. It does not, by itself, operate the long-lived production fleet.

answer.text: A Terraform state file describing the production fleet
An Ansible inventory containing all running servers
A custom AMI built using a temporary instance

questiontext.text: The lecture describes a problematic form of a “golden image.” What makes that example an anti-pattern?

generalfeedback.text: The problem is the unrepeatable manual creation process and accumulated hidden changes. The lecturer explicitly distinguishes this from an automated, rebuildable image that an organization may also call a “golden image.” The name alone is not the anti-pattern.

answer.text: The image was modified manually and cannot be reliably recreated from a maintained build definition.
The organization uses a shared base image.
The image has been tested before use.
The image is generated by an automated build pipeline.

questiontext.text: A team needs equivalent Ubuntu-based machines in two AWS regions and on both x86-64 and ARM64 processors. Which assumption is sound?

generalfeedback.text: Image selection must match the target region and CPU architecture. Equivalent image contents in different regions do not imply the same AMI ID.

answer.text: One AMI ID is valid in every region and on both architectures.
The VM instance type converts any image to the required architecture automatically.
The team must select suitable images for each region and architecture combination.
Only the size of the VM's disk determines whether the image can boot.

name.text: L2 Q5 Stock and custom images

questiontext.text: Explain the difference between a stock image and a custom image. Give one reason an organization would maintain a custom image instead of configuring every new machine entirely from a stock image at launch time.

graderinfo.text:
• 1 mark: A stock image is a supplied starting image, such as a distribution vendor's Ubuntu image; a custom image adds an organization's chosen software or configuration.
  • 1 mark: A relevant reason, such as consistently applying a security baseline, reducing repeated installation work, shortening launch time, or maintaining a tested organization-specific starting state.

name.text: L2 Q6 Build time and boot time

questiontext.text: Explain the difference between Packer provisioning during an image build and cloud-init configuration when a machine boots. Give one suitable example for each stage.

graderinfo.text:
• 1 mark: Packer provisioning prepares the image before it is reused, for example installing shared tooling or applying a common baseline.
  • 1 mark: Cloud-init can initialize an instance at boot using supplied metadata/user data, for example setting instance-specific configuration or running initial setup. It is not a general continuously running reconciliation loop; whether an individual action repeats depends on cloud-init configuration and module frequency.

Accept reasonable alternative placements if the student explains the trade-off between a larger prepared baseline and more work at launch.

name.text: L2 Q7 Containers and virtual machines

questiontext.text: Explain one important difference between a typical Linux container and a virtual machine in how they use the operating-system kernel. State one practical consequence for their isolation or compatibility.

graderinfo.text:
• 1 mark: Typical Linux containers share the host's Linux kernel, while VMs run a guest operating system with its own kernel over virtualized hardware.
  • 1 mark: A valid consequence: containers generally have a smaller startup/runtime overhead, share a kernel-level boundary, or require compatibility with the host kernel. VMs can provide different guest kernels. On a non-Linux desktop, Linux containers normally use a Linux VM underneath.

Do not accept “containers have no isolation” or “any container can run unchanged on any operating system and architecture.”

questiontext.text: A company needs web-server and database-server images with the same security baseline. Propose a simple image hierarchy and explain one maintenance benefit compared with independently repeating the baseline setup in every image build.

graderinfo.text:
• 1 mark: A suitable hierarchy is vendor Ubuntu → shared organization baseline → separate web and database images.
  • 1 mark: Shared baseline changes can be maintained centrally and reused, reducing duplicated provisioning logic and inconsistent baseline setup. Descendant images still need rebuilding and testing when the baseline changes; existing instances do not inherit the changes automatically.

name.text: L2 Q9 Reading the image build

questiontext.text:
demo-02/devops-ubuntu-26.04-aws.pkr.hcl defines two build sources:

source "amazon-ebs" "ubuntu-north" {
  region = "eu-north-1"
  # Other settings omitted
}

source "amazon-ebs" "ubuntu-west" {
  region = "eu-west-1"
  # Other settings omitted
}

# The build uses both sources. Its provisioning scripts include,
# in this order:
# cloud-init.sh, base.sh, git.sh, aws-cli.sh, motd.sh,
# disable-auto-updates.sh, cleanup.sh, zerodisk.sh

The first script waits for the initial cloud-init process to finish. The final scripts clean temporary files and prepare the disk before the image is captured.

  1. Describe the build lifecycle from source image to resulting AMI, including the role of the temporary VM and what happens to it after a successful build. (2 marks)
  2. Why does the build wait for cloud-init before changing the operating system, and why does cleanup belong after software installation? (2 marks)

graderinfo.text:
• 1 mark: For each configured source, Packer starts a temporary VM from the selected stock image and runs the provisioners against it.
  • 1 mark: It captures the prepared machine state as a custom AMI and, on normal successful completion, removes the temporary build instance. The two configured targets produce regional AMIs; the image artifacts remain available.
  • 1 mark: Waiting for cloud-init avoids racing initial configuration, package-manager activity, or related boot-time setup.
  • 1 mark: Final cleanup removes build-time leftovers after installation has finished, so temporary files and caches are not needlessly captured in the reusable image. Cleanup is not proof that every secret or machine-specific identity has been sanitized.

name.text: L2 Q10 Repeating a build and rolling out an update

questiontext.text:
The Packer template selects its source image using most_recent = true. Its base.sh script runs apt-get update and apt-get dist-upgrade. A student claims: “The code is in Git, so rebuilding next month is guaranteed to produce exactly the same software versions.”

  1. Assess that claim. Identify two inputs that can change without a change to the Git commit, and explain how to control them when reproducible versions are required. (2 marks)
  2. The team deliberately builds a patched image. Describe an immutable rollout to the running application, including validation and preservation of persistent data. (2 marks)

graderinfo.text:
• 1 mark: most_recent = true can resolve to a different source AMI later. Record or pin the approved source AMI for the relevant region/architecture when rebuilding the same version is required.
  • 1 mark: Package repositories and the versions selected by dist-upgrade can change. Control approved package versions and their availability, for example with a versioned repository snapshot or equivalent reproducible dependency source. Versioned build instructions alone do not freeze external inputs.
  • 1 mark: Build and validate the patched image, then create replacement instances and verify application health before directing traffic to them. Retain an appropriate recovery path until the replacement is proven.
  • 1 mark: Keep persistent application data on suitable separately managed storage or migrate/restore it through a tested procedure before retiring old instances. Running machines are not patched merely by publishing a new AMI.
